name: Helicar XT
description: Helicar XT is a helically-wound multi-wall carbon nanotube cable material produced through Apex Nanofabrication's continuous spin-deposition process, achieving tensile strengths exceeding 300 GPa — roughly forty times that of high-carbon steel at one-sixth the weight. Each strand consists of billions of aligned MWCNTs locked into a self-reinforcing helical geometry that distributes load across the entire cross-section rather than individual tubes. The result is a cable material that fails gracefully rather than catastrophically, giving audible warning before final fracture.
applications: structural tension members in arcology construction
story_hooks: A the Gray Zone district bridge is held up by counterfeit Helicar XT — visually identical but with a fraction of the rated strength. Someone knows, and someone is profiting.
Apex Nanofabrication's continuous spin-deposition line was sabotaged; every spool of Helicar XT produced in a three-week window has an invisible flaw that will cause failure under sustained load.
A black-market supplier is selling genuine Helicar XT salvaged from a demolished orbital platform — but the material has been stressed in ways that aren't detectable without specialized equipment.
